The Dark-eyed Junco is a variable bird characterized by its white outer tail feathers. Juveniles of all are streaky brown at first. "Slate-colored Junco" is the only form usually seen in the East. Unlike "Oregon Junco," sides and flanks are gray, not brown or tan. "Red-backed Junco" is resident in the mountains of northern Arizona and New Mexico, and seldom moves far from nesting areas.
